subject.title: Support session-level environment variables for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw expose per-spawn ACP session environment variables through `sessions_spawn.env`, or should operators use a different env surface such as configured per-agent env or trusted sandbox-env injection?
rationale: The request is useful but creates a model/tool-facing credential and runtime-control surface, so implementation needs maintainer intent on trust boundary, validation, redaction, persistence, and overlap with related env designs.

options.title: Design per-spawn ACP env
options.body: Add a credential-safe `sessions_spawn.env` contract with explicit validation/redaction and wire it through ACP/ACPX session creation.

options.title: Route users to per-agent env
options.body: Do not add per-call ACP env and instead use the configured `agents.list[].env` direction for operator-owned stable environment values once that lands.

options.title: Unify with trusted sandbox env
options.body: Defer this issue until the trusted per-call env-injection design decides a shared source-of-trust and safety model.

recommendation.title: Design per-spawn ACP env
recommendation.body: Add a credential-safe `sessions_spawn.env` contract with explicit validation/redaction and wire it through ACP/ACPX session creation.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP spawn/session surface appears to originate from their merged ACP thread-bound agent work.
